decisions.reason: As a large established specialist-lighting firm, we would keep this newly launched naval vessel system because its niche fit with our engineering capabilities and the lack of clear negative market evidence leave results too uncertain to justify an early exit.

We would keep this desk lamp because a dedicated product page suggests at least acceptable initial attention relative to aspiration and it uses familiar lighting and ergonomic competences with limited carrying risk for a large firm.

We would keep this newly arrived general interior luminaire because its own page and explicit launch messaging indicate it is still in the evaluation phase, and it fits the firm’s core building-lighting business and strategic move toward efficient modern solutions.

We would keep this pendant luminaire because, despite modest website prominence, it is close to our core office and building applications, so boundedly rational management would allow more time before concluding it falls below aspiration.

We would keep this marine HMI searchlight because specialist marine products often have long sales cycles, and with organisational slack we can continue testing market acceptance rather than redeploying resources immediately.

We would keep this marine searchlight because it is adjacent to our robust specialist-lighting business and there is no strong sign yet that performance is sufficiently below aspiration to trigger dropping it after only one year.
